_comment_not_in_battery: Several rules are verified outside this ART battery, all documented in phase-4-detection/sigma/README.md and proven by phase-4-detection/sigma/sigma-selftest.py: (1) T1105 certutil download (rules 100500/1) — Microsoft Defender kills certutil download before it spawns, so there's no telemetry (defense-in-depth, not a gap). (2) T1562.001 Defender exclusion via PowerShell (ps_script rule 100506) — this host's offline Atomic Red Team bundle has no T1562.001 atomic, so it was live-fired manually (Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath) to prove the ps_script->Wazuh path fires end-to-end, then the exclusion was removed. (3) T1560.001 (archive staging, rules 100517-519) — no offline-viable ART atomic exists (the rar/7-Zip/WinZip tests all require downloading the installer; the one self-contained test uses .NET ZipFile, not the Compress-Archive cmdlet the ps_script rule keys on) — validated instead via a direct Compress-Archive invocation in ad-validate.py. (4) T1047/T1021.006/T1569.002 (WMI/WinRM/PsExec lateral movement, rules 100513-516) and T1190 (DMZ web attack, rules 100440-442) aren't ws-01-local ART atomics at all — they're attacks launched FROM atk-01 (against ws-01 or dmz-01), so they live in ad-validate.py alongside the AD attack scenarios, which already models exactly that shape. (5) T1490 rule 100522 (wmic shadowcopy delete) — ART test 2 ('Windows - Delete Volume Shadow Copies via WMI') is correctly mapped, but wmic.exe does not exist on this ws-01 build (Windows 11 25H2 dropped it; verified 2026-09-06: Test-Path on both System32\\wmic.exe and System32\\wbem\\WMIC.exe returns False, Get-Command finds nothing) — an environment/tooling gap, not a rule defect; the rule's logic is unchanged and still correct for any host that has wmic. (6) T1003.001 comsvcs MiniDump (rules 100525/100526) — Microsoft Defender detects and removes the exact command line as Trojan:Win32/RundllLolBin.AF (ThreatID 2147793100, verified live 2026-09-06 via Get-WinEvent on the Windows Defender/Operational log) before rundll32.exe ever spawns, so there is no Sysmon process-create event to catch — same defense-in-depth class as T1105 certutil: the endpoint control is the outer layer, and this rule is the layer that catches the technique wherever that control is weakened, disabled, or bypassed. (Originally added specifically to survive LSASS PPL blocking the *read*; turns out Defender blocks the *launch* first in this lab's default config — a stricter finding than the one it was written for.) NOTE ON TEST NUMBERING: the ART test numbers actually on disk (`Invoke-AtomicTest T1490 -ShowDetailsBrief`) do not match the technique's public GitHub numbering 1:1 on this offline-installed copy — test 9 here is 'Disable System Restore Through Registry', not vssadmin resize (that's test 10). Confirmed by listing tests directly on ws-01, not by trusting a remembered/fetched number; the original T1490 entry above was off by one for exactly this reason before being fixed.
